title: Differential kernel selector and adaptive prefetch scheduler for multi‑GPU prefill/decode
creator: Marina Holt
description:
Problem: In heterogeneous multi-GPU prefill/decode scenarios the runtime currently picks kernels using a static priority table which leads to suboptimal choices for mixed sequence lengths, quantized models, and pipeline/tensor parallel boundaries. We observe tail latency spikes when the chosen kernel forces excessive cross-device communication during prefill, and wasted throughput when attention kernels are selected without accounting for upcoming decode patterns or KV cache reuse.

Goal: Implement a Differential Kernel Selector (DKS) combined with an Adaptive Prefetch Scheduler (APS) that jointly reasons about: kernel latency and throughput profiles, expected communication cost (NCCL) across pipeline/tensor partitions, KV cache hit probability, and downstream decode phase characteristics. The system should make per-request kernel and prefetch decisions, enable staged rollouts, and include observability for decision rationale.

Scope:
- DKS: runtime component that scores candidate kernels per operator (attention/mha, ffn) using a weighted model of on-device compute cost, expected NCCL cost, and quantization-accuracy penalty.
- APS: request-level prefetch window planner that determines when to prefetch KV shards to reduce stalls and when to delay/merge NCCL operations to maximize overlap with compute.
- Integration: hook DKS decisions into the multi-GPU scheduler so kernel choice can influence microbatch ordering and NCCL launch timing.
- Telemetry: surface per-decision metrics (selected_kernel, score_vector, estimated_comm_bytes, expected_latency) to Console and perf dashboards.

Non-goals: model re-training, changes to user-facing APIs, or permanent binary-only kernel additions (we will prefer parameterized kernels and knobs).
comments: 2026-02-16 - Sync: initial scope reviewed with runtime and infra. Agreed to prototype DKS as a thin scoring layer that queries an offline profile DB. Action: Marina to write perf profile schema (blocked until profile extraction job completes).

2026-02-20 - PRF: extracted per-kernel microbenchmarks across seq=32/256/1024 on A100/4xA100. Data uploaded to perf-db. Notable: fused attention (fp16) wins throughput for long seq but has higher single-step latency vs atten-lite kernel at short seqs.

2026-02-24 - Design decision: use a linear composite score: score = alpha * device_time + beta * comm_time + gamma * kv_miss_penalty + delta * quant_error_penalty. We will expose alpha/beta/gamma/delta as dynamically tunable runtime knobs. Diego will implement score evaluators; Marina will document reasoning and default weights.

2026-02-28 - Implementation note: APS prototype uses a conservative prefetch window of 3 tokens ahead for decode-heavy workloads to keep headroom for NCCL coalescing. Simulated run with synthetic traffic shows 7% P50 latency improvement and 18% throughput improvement for mixed batch sizes.

2026-03-03 - Review: PR 1387 submitted for DKS interface and profile loader. Feedback from SRE: need bounded memory for profile cache and eviction strategy. Diego: added LRU cache + TTL 6h. Marina: added metrics for cache hit ratio.

2026-03-05 - Interop: coordinated with pipeline scheduler (ENG-472501) to add a kernel_hint field to microbatch descriptors so the multi-stage conductor can reorder non-dependent microbatches to increase overlap. Early results: NCCL launch consolidation reduced PCIe bursts by ~22% in our lab tests.

2026-03-07 - Safety: turned off aggressive NCCL coalescing for customers with strict determinism needs. Added label to rollout config (deterministic_mode) and a fallback path that preserves original ordering.

2026-03-09 - Bench: end-to-end bench on 8xA100 w/ tensor+pipeline parallelism (tp=2, pp=4) using Llama-2-13B quantized shows throughput +20% and 95th P99 latency down ~12ms when DKS+APS enabled vs baseline. Need longer A/B run in staging before can enable for more customers.
2026-03-10 - Next steps: finish PR 1402 for APS NCCL coalescer, add canary (10% traffic) in dedicated, and create rollout checklist plus rollback metrics. Assigned Diego + SRE on canary monitoring.
benchmark_summary: 4xA100 mixed workloads: throughput +12-28% (seq 512-2048), P99 latency improvements 6-14ms on decode-heavy traces; staging canary (10%) shows reduced NCCL burstiness by 22% and LRU profile cache hit ~92%.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal perf lab validation (done). Phase 1: dedicated canary at 10% traffic for 48h with metrics: request_error_rate, p99_latency, tokens/sec, NCCL_coalesced_ops, profile_cache_hit. Phase 2: expand canary to 50% across two regions; Phase 3: gradual global rollout. Rollback triggers: >5% error rate increase, >10% p99 degradation vs baseline, or NCCL stall events > threshold.
open_risks: 1) Score model sensitivity: default weights may not generalize across hardware families. 2) Quantization accuracy penalty heuristics may misclassify micro workloads leading to quality regressions. 3) Increased decision latency for scoring (microseconds target) could negate gains if unbounded.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end canary shows tokens/sec uplift >=10% and p99 latency not worse than baseline for decode workloads. 2) No customer-facing quality regressions detected in evals tied to prod prompts. 3) Observability surfaces per-decision metrics and debug logging available behind a flag.
notes: Implementation uses existing kernel registry and adds the score evaluation as an orthogonal decision layer. APS uses a light-weight NCCL coalescing scheduler that only merges launches when it predicts compute overlap > 12ms. Follow-ups: add ML-trained ranking model (post-MVP), extend weights auto-tuning based on live latency feedback, and evaluate behavior for sparse attention kernels.
